stories.title: Jamia forms panel to draft students' union constitution as hunger strike continues
stories.body: Jamia Millia Islamia has formed a five-member committee to draft a constitution for a students' union, dissolved in 2006, PTI reported on Wednesday 21 October. Dean of Social Sciences Zubair Meenai chairs it, and the draft is due by 20 December. Students who have protested on campus since Monday 12 October rejected the move as a delaying tactic and say their indefinite hunger strike continues until an election schedule is announced. The university has designated a protest space, posted a medical team and an ambulance, and said disciplinary action taken up to 21 October would be reviewed, while any new action after 5.30 pm that day would draw strict measures.
stories.check: NEEDS CHECK: reports differ on the protest site (Outlook says a shelter inside Gate 7; PTI and Jamia's release say Ghalib Lawns) and on the hunger strike start (12 October in PTI and Outlook, 13 October in Careers360). Students' allegations of forcible removal on 17 October are unverified and are not addressed in Jamia's release. A seven-member high-level committee set up on 18 October (release 6161, 19 October) was missed in earlier briefs. Confirm current status with Jamia.

stories.title: Jamia's Foreign Languages department marks first Hangeul Day with international conference
stories.body: The Department of Foreign Languages at Jamia Millia Islamia celebrated its first Hangeul Day, the day of the Korean script, with an international conference on Thursday 15 and Friday 16 October, according to a university press release dated Wednesday 21 October. The inaugural session was held at the Engineering Auditorium under Vice-Chancellor Mazhar Asif, with a Korean Embassy minister among the guests. The release says the conference drew 45 researchers from six countries. On the second day students took part in Korean calligraphy, essay, poster, reels and singing contests, followed by cultural performances. The release says it should lay groundwork for future Korean Studies programmes.
stories.check: Single source (Jamia press release 6165). The release page shows only the headline; the details come from the English PDF. Confirm with Jamia.

stories.title: Jamia's Arabic department hosts extension lecture on teaching Arabic under NEP 2020
stories.body: Jamia Millia Islamia's Department of Arabic held an extension lecture on Wednesday 21 October at Mir Anees Hall, titled on reimagining Arabic teaching and learning in line with the National Education Policy 2020, according to a university press release of the same date. The speaker was the Regional Director of IGNOU's Delhi-1 Regional Centre. He urged moving from grammar-centred teaching to communication-oriented learning and said skills-based Arabic could improve employability in journalism, translation, interpretation and medical tourism. A former head of the Department of Adult and Continuing Education and Extension presided. Faculty, students and research scholars attended.

stories.title: Jamia's Psychology department observes World Mental Health Week with workshop, talks and awareness march
stories.body: Jamia Millia Islamia's Department of Psychology observed World Mental Health Week from Monday 12 to Wednesday 14 October under the theme "Lived Experiences Heard: Real Voices, Real Change", according to a university press release dated Wednesday 21 October. The Subject Association organised poster-making, a quiz, a street play, a Mental Health First Aid workshop led by a counselling psychologist and a film screening. Alumni gave talks on youth wellbeing, relationships and boundaries, and anxiety and depression. The week ended with an awareness march from the department at 10 am on 14 October, which the Chief Proctor attended.

stories.title: Jamia law students win national legal quiz competition
stories.body: Two final-year B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) students of Jamia Millia Islamia's Faculty of Law won first place at a National Legal Quiz Competition held at DGIM College, Faridabad, on Thursday 8 October, according to a university press release dated Wednesday 21 October. The release says the quiz had three rounds testing statutory knowledge, legal comprehension and strategic agility, with 48 competitors from institutions across India. The winners received a cash prize, a trophy and certificates. The Dean of the Faculty of Law praised their dedication.
